witnesses.separates: $TileParse from the concept: two pieces stand side by side on the same rows, so bg-free windows cross them.
$FillDefault and $BgDefault from the concept: the input has no mark-free piece, so no piece points to the center block.
$NeedsFill from the concept: a tenth 3x3 block has no fill cell. The concept places it at the center, where the mark-free piece already stands; $NeedsFill drops it.

$BboxCenter from the concept: the top piece has a T of marks whose stem reaches the bottom row. The mean of its marks lies above the piece center, and the center of their bounding box is the piece center.
$FillDerived from the concept: colors 5 and 3 are swapped in train0's input, so the pieces are filled with 3.
$SizeDerived from the concept: the pieces are 4x4. The stored size 3 reads four overlapping windows in each piece.

$BboxCenter and $EdgeTouch from the concept and $EdgeCount, when a block no piece points to is filled: the mark-free piece is missing, and the top piece's T of marks has a stem that reaches the bottom row. The mean of its marks sends the piece to the top block; the center of their bounding box, and the edges they touch, send it to the center block.
$NeedsFill from the concept: the center piece is solid 3, with no fill cell. The concept places it at the center block; $NeedsFill drops it and leaves the center block empty.

$EdgeCount and $EdgeTouch from the concept and $BboxCenter, at piece size 4: the top piece's marks are two cells on its second row, touching no edge. The mean of the marks and the center of their bounding box lie above the piece center; no mark lies on an edge line, so $EdgeCount and $EdgeTouch send the piece to the center block, where the mark-free piece stands.

$EdgeCount and $EdgeTouch from the concept and $BboxCenter, at piece size 4, when a block no piece points to is filled: bar-four without the mark-free piece. The mean and bounding-box readings place the bar piece in the top block; $EdgeCount and $EdgeTouch place it in the center block.

$FillDerived from the stored fill, when a block no piece points to is filled: the input holds three single cells and no piece. Every block is empty; the stored fill fills the output with 5, and the derived fill with 2.

$FillDerived from the stored fill, and $NeedsFill from the concept: the eight marked pieces stand beside six solid blocks of 7, and 7 is the most frequent color. At the stored fill the solid blocks are fill-free and share the center block; at the derived fill every 5-filled piece is all marks.
$SizeDerived from the stored size: the mark-free piece is a 4x4 square. At the stored size its four 3x3 squares all point to the center block; the derived size is 4, and the 3x3 pieces are not read.

$TileParse from the concept, and $SizeDerived from the stored size under $TileParse: four pieces stand as an aligned 2x2 block. The tile cut reads the four pieces; the bg-free squares crossing them break the window parse, and the derived size is 6.

$SkipUnmarked from the cases that place the mark-free piece, when a block no piece points to is filled: a tenth piece has one mark, at its center cell, so it points to the center block beside the mark-free piece. Dropping the mark-free piece leaves the marked piece alone at the center.
$SizeDerived from the stored size under $TileParse, at the derived bg: four-square on a wider field of 0, so that 0 is the most frequent color.
`bg=DominantColor` from the stored value: train 0 with 0 and 7 swapped
each case at the stored bg from its bg=DominantColor copy: the nine pieces stand one cell apart, so fill outnumbers bg and the derived bg is fill
